{{Short description|Natural number}}{{Notability|Numbers|date=July 2026}}{{Infobox number|number = 318}}

'''318''' ('''three hundred [and] eighteen''') is the natural number following 317 and preceding 319.  It has significance in [[Judaism]] and [[Christianity]].

==In Mathematics==
The number 318 has the proper divisors 1, 2, 3, 6, 53, 106, and 159.  It is an [[Abundant number|abundant]] number,<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Vanovschi |first=Vitalii |title=Properties of the number 318 |url=http://www.numberempire.com:80/318 |access-date=2026-08-26 |website=www.numberempire.com |language=en}}</ref> a [[sphenic number]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=Sloane's A007304 : Sphenic numbers |url=https://oeis.org/A007304 |website=The On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences |publisher=OEIS Foundation}}</ref> and a [[nontotient]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Sloane's A005277 : Nontotients |url=https://oeis.org/A005277 |access-date=2016-06-02 |website=The On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences |publisher=OEIS Foundation}}</ref> There are 318 posets with 6 unlabeled elements.<ref>{{cite OEIS|A000112|Number of partially ordered sets (posets) with n unlabeled elements}}</ref>

==In Religion==
The number 318 holds some significance in Judeo-Christian traditions and history. In the [[Talmud]], scholars interpret the number as a literal reference to the faithful servant, [[Eliezer]]. Using [[gematria]] (a Jewish alphanumeric code), the [[Hebrew]] letters in Eliezer’s name add up to 318.<ref>{{Cite book |title=The Babylonian Talmud |volume=Nedarim |chapter=32a |publisher=The Soncino Press |location=London |year=1936}}</ref>

In [[Greek numerals]], 318 is written as τιη. The letter Tau (τ) is interpreted as resembling the cross and the letters Iota (ι) and Eta (η) represent [[Jesus Christ]] as the first two letters in his name in Greek, Ἰησοῦς<ref>{{Cite web |title=Epistle of Barnabas, Chapter 9 |url=https://www.ccel.org/ccel/schaff/anf01.vi.ii.ix.html |website=Christian Classics Ethereal Library |access-date=2026-07-10 |language=en}}</ref>

In early [[Christian history]], the [[First Council of Nicaea]] is traditionally recorded as having exactly 318 bishops in attendance.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The First Ecumenical Council |url=https://www.oca.org/orthodoxy/the-orthodox-faith/church-history/fourth-century/the-first-ecumenical-council |website=Orthodox Church in America |access-date=2026-07-10 |language=en}}</ref> Additionally, in [[Genesis 14]], Abram (later [[Abraham]]) leads a rescue mission for his nephew [[Lot (biblical person)|Lot]] with exactly 318 trained men.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Abram’s 318 Men |url=https://theopolisinstitute.com/abrams-318-men/ |access-date=2026-07-10 |website=www.theopolisinstitute.com |language=en}}</ref>

==In other fields==
318 is a predicted [[magic number (physics)|magic number]] for [[neutrons]].<ref>
